query: Which methods most effectively propagate calibration and DIF uncertainty into hybrid ecosystem models and present credible scenario intervals?

response.query: Which methods most effectively propagate calibration and DIF uncertainty into hybrid ecosystem models and present credible scenario intervals?
response.answer: Monte Carlo simulations and Bayesian inference methods effectively propagate calibration and DIF uncertainty into hybrid ecosystem models, presenting credible scenario intervals. These techniques allow for robust uncertainty quantification and scenario analysis.

results.title: Federal Register :: Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program
results.content: Docket Title | Document ID | Comments || Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program: Standards for 2026 and 2027, Partial Waiver of 2025 Cellulosic Biofuel Volume Requirement, and Other Changes | [EPA-HQ-OAR-2024-0505-0002](https://www.regulations.gov/document/EPA-HQ-OAR-2024-0505-0002) | [1,986](https://www.regulations.gov/document/EPA-HQ-OAR-2024-0505-0002/comment) |  |. In this action, EPA is proposing the volume targets and applicable percentage standards for cellulosic biofuel, BBD, advanced biofuel, and total renewable fuel for 2026 and 2027.[[1](#footnote-1-p25785)]  We are also proposing a number of regulatory changes, including reducing the number of RINs generated for imported renewable fuel and renewable fuel produced from foreign feedstocks and removing renewable electricity as a qualifying renewable fuel under the RFS program (commonly referred to as eRINs). EPA is requesting comment on multiple aspects of this action, including the proposed volume requirements, our technical analyses supporting those volumes, our proposal to reduce the number of RINs generated for imported renewable fuels and renewable fuels produced from foreign feedstocks, the removal of renewable electricity as a qualifying renewable fuel under RFS program, and the other proposed regulatory amendments.

results.title: JPPTThe Journal of Pediatric Pharmacology and Therapeutics
results.content: OBJECTIVE The objective was to update the KIDs List, a list of drugs and excipients that are potentially inappropriate for use in pediatric patients, accounting for emerging pharmacologic agents and published evidence. METHODS A panel of 12 pediatric pharmacists from the Pediatric Pharmacy Association (PPA) evaluated primary, secondary, and tertiary literature; FDA Pediatric Safety Communications; the UpToDate Lexidrug database; and product information for drugs that may be considered potentially inappropriate for use in pediatric patients. 17 A comparable evidence-based list of drugs was published in 2020 that sought to bring a similar focus to unintended and preventable ADRs in the pediatric population, namely the Key Potentially Inappropriate Drugs in Pediatrics, or “KIDs List.” 18 The KIDs List has improved medication safety in pedi-atric patients through dissemination of evidence-based information, incorporation into information systems, and quality improvement initiatives. Clinician-scientists have used the KIDs List to identify medications associated with a high risk for ADRs at pediatric hospitals and health systems caring for pediatric patients.
